opportunities.program: Horizon Europe - Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions, Doctoral Networks (incl. Joint and Industrial Doctorates)
opportunities.deadline_text: MSCA WP 2026-2027 call table: 'Opening: 28 May 2026 Deadline(s): 24 Nov 2026'. Portal: 'The submission session is now available for: HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01-01'.
opportunities.funding_text: Call budget EUR 628.03 million. Unit contributions per doctoral candidate per person-month: living allowance EUR 4,250 (x country correction coefficient; Italy 93.8%), mobility allowance EUR 710, family allowance EUR 660 (if applicable); institutional: research, training and networking EUR 1,600 and management and indirect EUR 1,200. EU contribution capped at 540 person-months per network.
opportunities.duration: Action max 48 months (60 for Joint Doctorates); each fellowship 3-36 months (48 for Joint Doctorates).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Consortia of universities, research organisations, businesses and other socio-economic actors; at least three independent legal entities each in a different EU Member State/Associated Country, at least one in an EU Member State. Third-country organisations may participate (associated partners).
opportunities.eligible_countries: Beneficiaries: EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries (plus LMIC list per General Annex B); associated partners worldwide.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (international organisation headquartered in Italy) is deemed established in Italy for MSCA DN and, as an IO HQ'd in a Member State, is eligible for funding in 'Training and mobility' actions (General Annex B). It can therefore be a funded beneficiary that recruits and hosts doctoral candidates (and could count as one of the three MS/AC entities). It is not a degree-awarding body, so a partner university must enrol the candidates. CIAT (IO HQ in Colombia) is not covered by the IO clause and would participate as an associated partner hosting secondments in Colombia/Kenya/etc. Max 40% of EU contribution to one IO. Mobility rule for candidates recruited by an IO: not more than 12 of the last 36 months in the same appointing organisation.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Coordinator must be a beneficiary established in an EU Member State/AC (Bioversity qualifies under the IO deeming rule). Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: None on research location; secondments worldwide (incl. third countries) encouraged, up to half of the fellowship (except Joint/Industrial Doctorates).
opportunities.consortium_details: 'Applications must be submitted by a consortium including at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and with at least one of them established in an EU Member State.' 'Not more than 40.0% of the EU contribution may be allocated to beneficiaries in the same country or to a single International European Research Organisation (IERO) or international organisation.'
opportunities.eligible_activities: Doctoral training programmes: recruitment and research training of doctoral candidates, network-wide training, secondments, workshops; all research domains (bottom-up).
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Bottom-up: a network on EO/AI for climate-resilient agriculture or crop modelling would fit; but it funds doctoral candidates, not the researcher's own salary.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Multi-year (up to 48 months) salaried doctoral positions hosted at Bioversity Italy with secondments to Alliance hubs in LAC/Africa; strong EU partnership building.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Deadline 24 Nov 2026 leaves ~4.5 weeks; only realistic by joining an existing consortium already drafting a proposal. Better target: DN 2027 (deadline 23 Nov 2027, opens 26 May 2027).
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue only by joining an existing network as a beneficiary or associated partner before 24 Nov 2026; otherwise plan now for HORIZON-MSCA-2027-DN-01 (opens 26 May 2027, deadline 23 Nov 2027, EUR 645.99 M) with Bioversity as recruiting beneficiary.
opportunities.potential_partners: EU universities with digital-agriculture/EO doctoral schools (e.g., Wageningen, Univ. of Twente ITC, Univ. of Bonn, Sapienza/Tor Vergata, KU Leuven) plus agri-tech companies for Industrial Doctorates.
opportunities.next_action: Contact Bioversity grants office to confirm PIC status/LEAR and willingness to recruit doctoral candidates; post a partner-search request on the portal for DN 2026/2027 networks on EO/AI for agriculture.

opportunities.deadline_text: MSCA WP 2026-2027 call table: 'HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01 459.70 08 Sep 2027'; 'Opening: 07 Apr 2027 Deadline(s): 08 Sep 2027'. Portal status: Forthcoming.
opportunities.funding_text: Call budget EUR 459.70 million. Unit contributions per person-month: living allowance EUR 6,350 x country correction coefficient (Italy 93.8% = approx. EUR 5,956), mobility allowance EUR 710, family allowance EUR 660 (if applicable); institutional: research, training and networking EUR 1,000, management and indirect EUR 650. Indicative total for 24 months in Italy without family allowance approx. EUR 199,600 (own calculation from WP unit rates).
opportunities.duration: European Postdoctoral Fellowships: 12-24 months (plus optional up to 6-month non-academic placement).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Single host organisation (mono-beneficiary) in an EU Member State/AC applying jointly with a postdoctoral researcher of any nationality.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Host: EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Researcher: any nationality for European Fellowships (Global Fellowships require EU/AC nationals or long-term residents).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (IO HQ in Italy) is deemed established in Italy and may be the host/beneficiary that employs the fellow. Researcher eligibility: PhD awarded March 2024 (CV) -> well within 'maximum of 8 years' post-PhD. Colombian national -> eligible for a European (not Global) Fellowship. RISK: for IO hosts the mobility rule is 'not more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the call deadline, in the same appointing organisation'; the researcher has been employed by CIAT since Oct 2024. CIAT and Bioversity are separate legal entities but form one Alliance, so REA must be consulted on whether Bioversity counts as a different 'appointing organisation'. Fallback: host at an EU university/research centre (mobility rule then applies to the host country, e.g., not resident in Italy/Germany/NL >12 of last 36 months, which the researcher meets). CIAT (Colombia) cannot be the beneficiary.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: 'Applications must be submitted by a single independent legal entity, established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.' 'The beneficiary must employ and supervise the researcher during the action.'
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Fellowship hosted in EU MS/AC; secondments allowed in any country worldwide.
opportunities.consortium_details: Mono-beneficiary action; associated partners only for secondments/placements.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Individual research and training project in any field, with career development plan, secondments and optional non-academic placement.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Bottom-up individual fellowship: an EO + AI + crop modelling project (e.g., foundation-model-based crop yield forecasting for climate adaptation) fits directly.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Funds the researcher's own salary for up to 2 years at an EU host, building EU network/visibility; Bioversity hosting would keep the work within the Alliance.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Researcher meets career-stage criteria; 10-page proposal; main uncertainty is the IO mobility-rule interpretation for Bioversity.
opportunities.recommendation: Strong candidate for the researcher's own salary. Decide host by early 2027: ask REA/Italian NCP (APRE) whether a CIAT employee can be recruited by Bioversity International under the IO mobility rule; if not, choose an EU university host with Bioversity/CIAT as secondment partner.
opportunities.potential_partners: Bioversity International (Rome/Maccarese) as host; alternatives: Wageningen University, Univ. of Twente ITC, Univ. of Bonn, JRC-linked groups; secondment at CIAT Cali.
opportunities.next_action: Email REA MSCA helpdesk/APRE with the mobility-rule question (CIAT employee -> Bioversity host); identify supervisor at Bioversity Italy; start proposal drafting in Q1 2027 ahead of 7 Apr 2027 opening.

opportunities.funding_text: Call budget EUR 51.32 million. 'The EU contribution is limited to EUR 10 million per beneficiary for this call.'
opportunities.duration: EU-funded phase 24-36 months + beneficiary-funded phase 24 months; fellowships of 48 or 60 months; action max 60 months (48-month fellowships) or 72 months (60-month fellowships).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: 'Applications must be submitted by a single entity established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.' Implementing partners must also be in MS/AC.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Beneficiary and implementing partners: EU Member States / Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Recruited researchers: any nationality.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Bioversity International (IO HQ in Italy) is 'deemed to be established' in Italy and could be the single beneficiary running a postdoc recruitment programme (min. 3 researchers). It must guarantee funds for the 24-month self-funded phase. Researchers 'already permanently employed by the organisation hosting them cannot be funded'; IO mobility rule (max 12 of last 36 months in the same appointing organisation) applies. CIAT cannot be beneficiary or implementing partner (not in MS/AC).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Single beneficiary; 'The beneficiary will be responsible for the availability of the necessary complementary funds to implement the proposal and ensure the coverage of the phase fully funded by the beneficiary'; at least three researchers recruited within first 12 months.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Researchers hosted in MS/AC; secondments allowed.
opportunities.consortium_details: Single beneficiary, optional implementing partners in MS/AC.
opportunities.cofunding_details: Two-phase model: EU-funded phase 24-36 months; 'a phase funded fully by the beneficiary (24 months) in which the applicant is expected to set salaries attractive at a national level and ensure availability of the necessary internal or external funds'.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Institutional talent-recruitment programmes for postdoctoral researchers with open, merit-based international selection, career development and training.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Discipline-open programme; Bioversity could focus it on climate/landscapes/digital agriculture, but it is an institutional, not project, instrument.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Directly funds multi-year (48-60 month) postdoctoral positions in Italy - exactly the staff/long-term objective - but requires institutional commitment.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires Bioversity management decision and secured co-funding for 24 months per fellow by April 2027.
opportunities.recommendation: Raise with Alliance leadership/Bioversity Italy grants office as an institutional option for building an EO/AI postdoc cohort; only viable with committed matching funds.
opportunities.potential_partners: Bioversity International (beneficiary); Italian universities as implementing partners.
opportunities.next_action: Brief Bioversity research-management on the scheme before 8 Dec 2026 opening; estimate co-funding need (24 months x >=3 postdocs).

opportunities.deadline_text: Portal: opening 2026-10-06, single-stage deadline 2027-02-16; 'The submission session is now available for: HORIZON-BRIDGING-2027-04-03, HORIZON-BRIDGING-2027-04-11, HORIZON-BRIDGING-2027-04-08'.
opportunities.funding_text: Research and Innovation Action; topic budget EUR 10 million, 1 grant expected (EU contribution EUR 10 million).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Standard Horizon Europe consortium (General Annex B). Entities with commercial interest in SRM deployment should be avoided (conflict of interest).
opportunities.eligible_countries: EU MS/AC and LMICs in General Annex B list (incl. Colombia) eligible for funding; others as associated partners.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No topic-specific clause for international organisations. Under General Annex B, IOs HQ'd in a Member State (Bioversity) are funded only for training-and-mobility actions 'or when provided for in the specific call/topic conditions'; otherwise only 'if their participation is considered essential'. So Bioversity/CIAT would most likely join as associated partners (unfunded) or through a funded EU/Colombian university partner, unless the granting authority accepts them as essential.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Coordinator must be an eligible funded beneficiary; min. 3 independent entities from 3 different MS/AC (one in a MS).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Global scope; must use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS where satellite EO is used.
opportunities.consortium_details: Transdisciplinary consortium; global steering/advisory board with civil-society engagement required; EU representatives sit in evaluation committee.
opportunities.eligible_activities: EO-based detection/attribution of SRM activities, aerosol-cloud modelling (SAI, MCB, CCT), knowledge on SRM-induced changes to ecosystems, precipitation, light quality and net primary production, governance research. Field experiments and SRM technology development are out of scope.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Connects to the researcher's Degrees Initiative work on SAI impacts on maize/rice and EO skills; topic is mostly atmospheric/governance with an ecosystem-impact component.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Single EUR 10M grant; an agricultural-impact work package (crop/NPP response to SAI scenarios in LAC) could be a niche contribution.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Highly competitive single award; Alliance funding eligibility uncertain; must join a European-led consortium quickly.
opportunities.recommendation: Worth a targeted outreach to European SRM/climate-modelling groups forming consortia, offering a crop/terrestrial-impact WP; do not lead.
opportunities.potential_partners: European climate-modelling centres and universities active in SRM research; Degrees Initiative network; a funded Colombian university partner if CIAT cannot be funded.
opportunities.next_action: Search the portal partner-search for this topic and contact likely coordinators by Dec 2026.

opportunities.eligible_countries: EU MS/AC + LMICs (General Annex B list, incl. Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, etc.); scope focuses on African countries.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: No IO clause in topic conditions: Bioversity/CIAT funded only if deemed essential, otherwise associated partners. African national partners (universities, innovation hubs) can be funded beneficiaries. IA funding rate up to 100% for non-profits.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Min. 3 independent entities from 3 different MS/AC (one in a MS).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Living labs/deployment in low- and middle-income countries, focus on Africa.
opportunities.consortium_details: Should link to AI for Public Good, GenAI for Africa, Digital for Development Hub, Global Gateway; living labs in local innovation hubs.
opportunities.eligible_activities: TRL 5->7 prototyping, testing, validation and demonstration of locally adapted AI solutions trained on local data; living labs; talent pipelines; areas include 'climate and agriculture, biodiversity'.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: AI tools adapted with local data for agriculture/climate in Africa match the digital-advisory and geospatial-AI profile.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Small (EUR 1.5M) but directly on AI-for-agriculture in Africa; good for Alliance Africa hubs with African partners as funded beneficiaries.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance has relevant AI/advisory tools at TRL 5+; funding route for Alliance staff uncertain.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue as partner with an EU coordinator and African innovation hubs; clarify early with the EC whether Bioversity can be a funded beneficiary as 'essential'.
opportunities.potential_partners: EU AI research groups in AI-for-Public-Good/GenAI4Africa projects; African innovation hubs (e.g., in Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana); Alliance Africa hub.
opportunities.next_action: Read full topic when it opens 17 Nov 2026; identify EU coordinator and African hubs by Jan 2027.

evidence.eligibility_quote: General Annex B: International organisations with headquarters in a Member State or Associated Country are eligible to receive funding for 'Training and mobility' actions or when provided for in the specific call/topic conditions. Other international organisations are not eligible to receive funding, unless provided for in the specific call/topic conditions, or if their participation is considered essential for implementing the action by the granting authority.
evidence.staff_costs_quote: General Annexes, Budget categories: 'actual costs (i.e. costs which are real and not estimated or budgeted) for: - personnel costs (unless declared as a unit cost ...)'; 'The maximum Horizon Europe funding rates are as follows: - Research and innovation action: 100% - Innovation action: 70% (except for non-profit legal entities, where a rate of up to 100% applies)'. Topic conditions: 'Eligible costs will take the form of a lump sum' (lump sum is fixed from a detailed budget table that includes personnel).

opportunities.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship for Postdocs (next call opens 15 Nov 2026)
opportunities.funder: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (funded by the German Federal Government)
opportunities.deadline_text: Page: 'We have received the maximum number of applications for the current call.' Next call opens November 15, 2026. Three calls per year (15 March, 15 July, 15 November); 'Once a call has reached the maximum number of currently 800 applications, the application round will be closed.'
opportunities.funding_text: Postdocs: EUR 3,000 per month plus additional benefits; experienced researchers: EUR 3,600 per month.
opportunities.duration: Postdocs 6-24 months (can be split into up to three stays within three years).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Individual researchers (non-German) with doctorate completed within the last four years (postdocs) or twelve years (experienced), with a host at a German university or research institution.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Any nationality except German nationals (with exceptions); research conducted in Germany.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Individual fellowship: the Alliance is not an applicant or host. The researcher personally qualifies (PhD March 2024 < 4 years; Colombian national; check <90 days in Germany in last 18 months). Funds the researcher's stipend at a German host (e.g., Univ. of Bonn, Hohenheim, PIK, ZALF); Alliance could be a collaborating partner. Would require leave/secondment from CIAT. [Ingest note 2026-10-22: individual fellowship — the researcher may qualify personally, but the Alliance is not an applicant and research must be carried out at a host in Germany; recorded as potentially_eligible.]
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Applicant + German host researcher (host statement, mentoring agreement, facilities confirmation).
opportunities.eligible_activities: Self-chosen research project at the German host institution.
opportunities.required_documents: Not specified on the page beyond host's statement, mentoring agreement and confirmation of facilities; see foundation's application guidelines.
opportunities.application_procedure: Online application when a call window is open (first-come until 800-application cap).
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Open-topic fellowship; an EO/AI crop-modelling project with a German agri-geospatial group fits.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Pays the researcher for up to 24 months but moves the work to Germany rather than funding Alliance staff.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Researcher meets criteria; individual proposal; needs a German host agreement before the window opens.
opportunities.recommendation: Good personal-career option if a German host is secured; apply on 15 Nov 2026 opening day or in the March/July 2027 windows because windows close at 800 applications.
opportunities.potential_partners: University of Bonn (remote sensing / crop modelling), University of Hohenheim, PIK Potsdam, ZALF Muencheberg.
opportunities.next_action: Identify German host and prepare documents before the 15 Nov 2026 window (or 15 Mar 2027).
